app.name: qcr-workbench
app.description: Local-first React SPA for FAIR-based quantitative cyber risk analysis. v2 adds a thin stateless Cloudflare Worker (edge assets + a public no-auth MCP server + optional Workers AI proxy); user data stays local-first (D1 dormant).
dataStores: IndexedDB (AES-256-GCM encrypted via passphrase-derived vault key; PBKDF2-SHA256 250k iterations)
localStorage (theme, store registry, auto-lock minutes, qcr.webmcp opt-in flag — no secrets by design)
Cloudflare D1 (qcr-workbench-db; schema present but data path largely unimplemented/dormant)
app.authModel: Passphrase-derived vault key (PBKDF2 -> AES-GCM) for local data; no accounts. Worker API rows scoped by Cf-Access-Authenticated-User-Email header (falls back to dev@localhost when absent). The /mcp server is public and unauthenticated by design (read-only pure-function tools).
thirdPartyServices: Anthropic / OpenAI / Gemini / Qwen / Cerebras / Ollama (user-supplied keys in the encrypted vault, opt-in, browser-direct)
Cloudflare Workers AI (keyless, via the Worker /api/ai proxy)
WebLLM model weights (CDN download, user-initiated on-device inference)
trustBoundaries: User free-text fields (scenario/treatment/assumption text) rendered back into the UI and into the exported executive report
Imported/restored backup files and imported scenario CSVs
Responses from AI providers (untrusted model output rendered as narrative)
App data composed into LLM prompts, including bundled reference content retrieved for grounding (prompt-injection surface)
The user-supplied Ollama base URL (arbitrary request destination / SSRF-shaped)
The public unauthenticated /mcp JSON-RPC endpoint and its tool arguments (worker/mcp.js, src/lib/mcp/tools.js)
Worker HTTP surface: /api/ai proxy and /api/projects D1 access keyed off the Cf-Access-Authenticated-User-Email request header
WebMCP tools registered in-page via navigator.modelContext when qcr.webmcp is enabled

ignoreNote: Test directories (__tests__, e2e) are excluded from the static scan: this app's FAIR Monte Carlo uses `iterations: <n>` counts that collide with the KDF-iteration rule, producing false positives, and test files do not ship to production. The real PBKDF2 site (src/lib/localdb/crypto.js, 250k iterations) is in scope and correctly passes. i18n/sample-data/knowledge-base files are excluded as static reference content, not executable logic.

dynamic.startCommand: npm run build && npm run preview -- --host 127.0.0.1 --port 4173 --strictPort
dynamic.baseUrlNote: Drives the PRODUCTION preview build: the CSP is injected only at build time (vite.config.js cspMetaPlugin), so header/CSP checks against `npm run dev` would be meaningless.
dynamic.setupFlowNote: Empty: post-unlock checks do not run. To enable them, add ordered steps matching this app's create-store/vault screen, e.g. {"action":"fill","selector":"input[type=password]","value":"$CANARY_PASS"} then {"action":"click","selector":"button:has-text('Create')"}. A full page reload re-locks the vault (module-level key) by design, so any flow must stay client-side.
